owner_decision: September 10, 2026: the site tracks PJM, ERCOT, MISO and SPP (the grid operators named in the news cluster that motivated this work) plus the national EIA figure as a fifth reference row. This task's network scope covers only the Federal Register API and the EIA API v2, so none of the four operators' own hosts (pjm.com, ercot.com, misoenergy.org, spp.org) were fetched; every reviewed source_url below was found by web research, not by the importer, and is a citation only until a machine-readable route is confirmed and approved for that host. No number from a PDF or spreadsheet is hand-entered into the ledger.

operators.name: PJM Interconnection
operators.note: PJM's annual Load Forecast Report (20-year peak-load forecast by zone, region and LDA) is published as a PDF; PJM's machine-readable planning data (Data Miner 2) requires a separate registered account and is outside this task's allowed network hosts. No number entered. Curated LAS planning figure (up to ~30 GW data-center growth 2025–2030) added 2026-09-22 as pjm-datacenter-growth-2025-2030-gw; full LTF peak-path import remains open. Curated 2026 Load Report summer-peak path added 2026-09-22 as pjm-rto-summer-peak-mw (2036=222,106 MW; 2046=253,077 MW); firm/non-firm derate language in event pjm-2026-ltf-large-load-firm-nonfirm. LAS ~30 GW figure remains separate.

operators.name: ERCOT
operators.note: ERCOT's Long-Term Load Forecast (hourly, 10-year) is published as a PDF report and stakeholder deck under ercot.com/gridinfo/load/forecast; no keyless CSV/JSON export was identified within this task's allowed network hosts. No number entered. Curated LLI queue observations from the Dec 2025 constraints report (~239 GW) and Apr 2026 board deck (~410 GW as of 2026-03-26) were added 2026-09-22 as ercot-large-load-queue-gw; long-term load-forecast PDF import remains open. Curated TSP vs studied 2031 peaks added 2026-09-22 as ercot-tsp-peak-forecast-2031-gw (218) and ercot-studied-peak-2031-gw (159) from the Dec 2025 constraints report.

operators.name: MISO
operators.note: MISO's long-term load forecast and its large-load-addition figures (e.g. MTEP's tracked large-load MW) are published as PDF whitepapers and MTEP report chapters under misoenergy.org; no keyless CSV/JSON export was identified within this task's allowed network hosts. No number entered. Curated Dec 2024 LTLF whitepaper peaks and incremental DC energy added 2026-09-22 as miso-coincident-peak-ltlf-gw (122 GW 2024; 152–186 GW 2044) and miso-datacenter-energy-twh. News 163 GW-by-2035 remains held.

operators.name: Southwest Power Pool
operators.note: SPP's peak-load growth projection (its ITP report cites roughly 56 GW current peak load rising toward 109 GW within a decade) is published as a PDF; no keyless CSV/JSON export was identified within this task's allowed network hosts. No number entered. Curated 2025 ITP figures added 2026-09-22: spp-peak-load-itp-gw (56→109 GW narrative) and spp-itp-coincident-peak-gw (Fig 2.1: 61.7/66.5/69.8/76.4). Keep narrative vs Fig 2.1 separate.

operators.name: United States (EIA, national)
operators.note: No confirmed EIA API v2 route for a national peak-load or large-load forecast was identified without a registered key; the Annual Energy Outlook's electricity-demand tables are the leading candidate. scripts/import_eia.py already imports EIA's Short-Term Energy Outlook total-generation series (eia-steo-generation-outlook) as national annual context; a dedicated grid_peak_load_forecast_mw series needs the key plus a live route check (the same 'confirm before first --apply' discipline already used for STEO_SERIES_ID) before it is added.
